title: Claims Manual: Settling Direct Losses Under CondoGuard
content:
Claims manual section for direct losses under the CondoGuard Unit-Owners Policy.

## 1. Coverage period

A direct loss is covered only when the date of loss falls within a term during which the policy was in force.

## 2. Unit property by master policy type

Coverage A pays unit property according to the association's master policy type:

| Master policy type | Original fixtures | Owner improvements |
|---|---|---|
| bare walls | paid | paid |
| single entity | denied, master policy primary | paid |
| all-in | denied, master policy primary | denied, master policy primary |

A class not paid is denied with the reason master policy primary, because the association's master policy insures it.

## 3. Deductible and payment basis

- One deductible applies per occurrence, absorbed first by unit property, then by personal property.
- Where the replacement-cost amount of a coverage part is at or below the tier's no-holdback threshold, the payment is replacement cost in full: the replacement-cost amount less the deductible applied.
- Otherwise the first payment is the actual-cash-value initial payment, the replacement-cost amount less the depreciation and less the deductible applied, with the depreciation withheld in one holdback entry; except personal property on a tier that settles Coverage C at actual cash value, which is paid as a final actual-cash-value payment with nothing withheld.

## 4. Limits and denials

- Theft of jewelry, watches and furs, of firearms, and of money is capped at the tier's special limits.
- Water backup is paid up to the policy's water backup limit, and denied with the reason no water backup coverage when that limit is 0.
- Surface water is denied with the reason surface water.
- Property and liability losses arising from renting the unit to others are denied with the reason rented without endorsement unless the occupancy on the policy is rented to others.

## 5. Payees, voids and closing

- A unit property payment of 5000.00 USD or more names the mortgagee as co-payee when one is on file.
- A payment that has already been voided is never voided again, as the claim records show; a claim is closed once every part is paid or denied and no holdback remains.

## Payment worksheet (hypothetical claim)

Bare walls master policy, tier no-holdback threshold 2500 USD, unit property replacement-cost amount 8000 USD, depreciation 1500 USD, deductible 1000 USD. The replacement-cost amount is above the threshold, so the first payment is 8000 less 1500 less 1000, that is 5500 USD, and 1500 USD is withheld. The payment is 5000.00 USD or more, so a mortgagee on file is named as co-payee. Had the replacement-cost amount been 2000 USD, the payment would have been 2000 less 1000, that is 1000 USD, with nothing withheld.
